sections.title: What the published book addresses
sections.text: Stiny connects visual calculation in shape grammars with art and design, using Coleridge’s contrast between imagination and fancy to frame the discussion.

sections.title: The stated premise
sections.text: The publisher describes imagination as seeing that can reorganize a whole, in contrast to rearranging already fixed units. Shape grammars are presented as a way for calculation to accommodate changing appearances.

sections.title: What is reported about the approach
sections.text: The description brings together shape-rule reasoning, literary ideas and visual examples to challenge accounts of creativity based only on predetermined descriptions. This identifies the author’s argument, not a controlled experiment.

sections.title: What still requires the final text
sections.text: Detailed examples, derivations, qualifications and conclusions were not checked in the 2022 publication. Claims about exceeding computer-based accounts should be read in their precise context rather than treated here as a proved complexity theorem.

sections.title: Version and reading route
sections.text: Use the publisher’s open-access link for this 2022 book. The earlier course collection has a different title and manuscript status; it provides related material but cannot verify the final book’s exact wording or organization.
